_notes.how_to_use: Replace every FILL_ME with a real value. train_lora.py refuses to run while any placeholder remains. 'layers_to_transform' may stay null (adapt all layers) or be a list of layer indices. 'target_modules' is a list of module-name suffixes.

original_paper_open_models_train_json.source: emergent-misalignment/open_models/train.json (Betley et al. 2025, arXiv:2502.17424). Model there is unsloth/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct.
original_paper_open_models_train_json.other: epochs 1, per_device_train_batch_size 2, grad_accum 8, lr 1e-5, warmup_steps 5, adamw_8bit, weight_decay 0.01, linear schedule, max_seq_length 2048, train_on_responses_only true

model_organisms_turner_et_al_2025.source: arXiv:2506.11613 'Model Organisms for Emergent Misalignment' (Turner, Soligo, Taylor, Rajamanoharan, Nanda), Appendix E Table 6 'Default LoRA Fine-tuning Parameters'; code at https://github.com/clarifying-EM/model-organisms-for-EM (em_organism_dir/finetune/sft/default_config.json).

default_all_adapter_lora.epochs: paper text (Sec. 3.4 footnote 6) says baseline results used alpha 64 and lr 1e-5 'across two epochs'; the released default_config.json has epochs=1. Ambiguous -- pick deliberately.

minimal_rank1_organism.note: Paper Sec. 3.5: single rank-1 adapter on the MLP down-projection of layer 24 of the 48-layer Qwen2.5-14B. The repo's single_adapter_config.json uses the same shape on Llama-3.2-1B with alpha 512 and lr 2e-5, so alpha is model-dependent. Layer 24 is ~half depth of a 48-layer model; for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (28 layers) the analogous layer is ~14.

model_organisms_turner_et_al_2025.caveat: Neither the paper nor the repo names Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct explicitly. They sweep Qwen2.5 from 0.5B to 32B, Llama-3.1/3.2 1B-70B and Gemma-3 up to 12B, all instruct variants, with the same default table. Treat the defaults above as the intended setting for 7B, not a measured one.

_notes.notes_on_rslora: Both works use rank-stabilized LoRA (scaling alpha/sqrt(r) instead of alpha/r). With r=32, alpha=64: rsLoRA scale = 64/sqrt(32) ~= 11.3, plain LoRA scale = 2.0. This is a large difference -- keep use_rslora consistent with whichever lr you copy.
